title: Consumer Acceptance of Reduced Salt and Nitrite Pepperoni Formulations Produced Using Novel Functional Starter Cultures
content:
Consumer acceptance represents a critical determinant of whether technologically successful food reformulation can progress towards commercial application. Although microbiological and processing strategies can support reductions in sodium chloride and nitrite without compromising the safety or physicochemical quality of fermented meats, it remains necessary to establish whether such reformulations preserve the sensory characteristics valued by consumers. This study therefore evaluated consumer acceptance of six pepperoni formulations comprising three conventional controls and three reduced-additive products previously characterised through trained descriptive sensory analysis. Consumers (n=128) evaluated appearance, aroma, flavour, texture, saltiness, spiciness and aftertaste using a seven-point hedonic scale. Overall preference, purchase intent and forced product ranking were also assessed. Differences among formulations were evaluated using Friedman tests followed by Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank comparisons.
Significant formulation effects were identified for all seven hedonic at-tributes, although effect sizes were small. Texture and appearance produced the greatest consumer differentiation, consistent with the prominence of structural and visual characteristics in the trained sen-sory analysis. Overall preference and purchase intent also differed sig-nificantly among formulations, but their small effect sizes and selective pairwise differences indicated limited consensus across consumers. CL.1, containing 0.5% salt and 50ppm nitrite, achieved the strongest performance among the reduced-additive formulations. Its over-all-preference and purchase-intent responses did not differ significantly from those of any conventional control, and it received more favourable responses than the formulations containing 10-25ppm nitrite across several outcomes. Forced ranking identified L.0 as the preferred for-mulation, while CL.1 remained within the broader competitive range of the products evaluated. Frequency distributions additionally demon-strated substantial heterogeneity in individual consumer responses, particularly for saltiness and product ranking. 
Together, the trained and consumer evaluations provided complemen-tary evidence that structural and visual characteristics were the clearest sensory consequences of reformulation, while many flavour-related at-tributes remained favourably accepted. The findings demonstrate that an integrated starter-culture and hurdle-based strategy can support substantial simultaneous reductions in salt and nitrite without produc-ing a consistent loss of consumer acceptance. CL.1 consequently pro-vides a promising reduced-additive formulation for subsequent indus-trial, shelf-life and market-based validation.
